prompt: I ran Louvain community detection on my co-authorship network (1200 authors, 4800 edges) and got 8 communities. The modularity is 0.67 which seems great. How do I report these communities in my paper? I want to name them and describe what each one represents.
assertions: Output warns that a single Louvain run is not 'the' partition — modularity degeneracy means many solutions have near-equal quality
Output recommends running community detection many times (e.g., 100+ runs) and measuring stability/consensus
Output mentions NMI (Normalized Mutual Information) or AMI or a similar stability metric for comparing partitions
Output does NOT recommend simply reporting the single-run partition without stability analysis
Output mentions Louvain resolution limit or the alternative of SBM (Stochastic Block Model) for more principled partitioning
